issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares a boolean attribute named 'excellentEnough' in ExcellenceLand, but the solution implementation declares the boolean as 'isExcellent' with a getter isExcellent(). This name mismatch means the implemented getter does not match the attribute name expected by the UML/tests (which will likely expect isExcellentEnough() or getExcellentEnough()), causing students or automated checks to observe inconsistent attribute/getter naming.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the boolean attribute name with the UML: rename the field in ExcellenceLand to 'excellentEnough' (private boolean excellentEnough) and provide the corresponding getter (e.g., public boolean isExcellentEnough()). Ensure the constructor parameter order and assignments use 'excellentEnough' (double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides) so the attribute name and getter match the UML and tests.
